slides.say: Given: x plus seven, in absolute value, is equal to nine. Which of the following could be the value of x?
So we have an equation with an absolute value, and all the choices are numbers. We'll solve it three ways, two cases, the number line, and plugging in the answers.
[short pause] Our first method, two cases. Remember, which numbers have an absolute value of nine? Nine, and negative nine. So the inside, x plus seven, is nine, or it's negative nine.
First case, x plus seven is nine. To get x alone, I take seven off both sides, and x is two.
Second case, x plus seven is negative nine. Take seven off again, and x is negative sixteen.
[short pause] Now careful with the choices. Is two there? No. But negative two is there, and that's the trap. It looks like our two, but it's a different number.

Negative sixteen is there, it's number three. And look at the wording, could be. Two values work, two and negative sixteen, but they only offer one of them. So negative sixteen, number three is our answer.

[pause] Our second method, the number line. Here we read the bars as a distance. Let's start with an easier one. The absolute value of x minus five is seven. Bars around a difference give the distance between two numbers, so this says x is seven steps away from five. Seven steps to the right, five plus seven is twelve. Seven steps to the left, five minus seven is negative two. So x is twelve, or negative two.
at: The absolute value of x minus five
five minus seven is negative two

slides.say: Now, what about a plus? x plus seven is x minus negative seven, because taking away negative seven is the same as adding seven. So the absolute value of x plus seven is the distance between x and negative seven. And it's nine, so x is nine steps away from negative seven. Nine steps to the right, negative seven plus nine is two. Nine steps to the left, negative seven minus nine is negative sixteen. Two isn't in the choices, but negative sixteen is, choice number three.
at: x plus seven is x minus
So the absolute value of x plus seven

slides.say: [pause] And our third method, plugging in the answers. The choices are numbers, so let's just try them. Sixteen plus seven is twenty-three, and twenty-three isn't nine, so no. Negative two plus seven is five, and five isn't nine, so no again.
Negative sixteen plus seven is negative nine, and its absolute value is nine. It works. In the exam you'd circle it and move on.
